- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next period.  
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp drop or mean reversion, reduce forecast slope by 10–30% to account for volatility.  
- After a price spike (e.g., >95), model often overshoots and continues upward; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use exponential decay to smooth out momentum.  
- When sentiment is high (≥0.4) and model is flat or slightly rising, expect mean reversion; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast to reflect potential correction.  
- If true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 3–5 days, assume lag or misalignment; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average or sentiment-weighted moving average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if model is consistently >95 and true outcome is <90, apply downward correction of 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in upward bias.
